items.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) and foundation models (FMs) are reshaping petroleum engineering at a pace no previous wave of artificial intelligence has matched. Between 2022 and 2026 the field went from zero petroleum specific LLMs to eighteen domain-specialized models, more than a dozen subsurface foundation models, and more than twenty commercial industry platforms, while annual publication counts grew more than five-fold from 2020 to 2024. This survey integrates those developments into a single framework. We analyze 296 verified references spanning 2003–2026 across 14 thematic areas and six petroleum sub-disciplines plus one cross-cutting category (geophysics, drilling, reservoir, production, petrophysics, completions, and cross-cutting), from classical natural-language-processing baselines through today’s vision–language models, retrieval-augmented generation stacks, and autonomous agents. Our organizing contributions include (i) a positioning matrix against 25 prior surveys, (ii) a bubble-plot taxonomy of sub-disciplines against AI paradigms, (iii) seven application-category tables, six additional thematic tables, and a dedicated maturity-model table (fourteen tables in total), (iv) a catalog of public petroleum AI systems and enabling substrate, and (v) the PetroLLM Maturity Model — a five-level scaffold (L1 Conversational Q&amp;A, L2 Document Intelligence and Retrieval, L3 Domain-Specialized LLMs, L4 Autonomous Agents and Copilots, L5 Self-Improving Foundation-Model Ecosystems) that situates every surveyed system on a common ladder. The paper closes with a bibliometric snapshot (trends, sub-discipline distribution, method distribution, institutional footprint) and an open-research agenda spanning data, benchmarks, physics integration, safety, multilinguality, and standards. Our headline findings: geophysics leads, reservoir and production lag, petroleum benchmarks are scarce, industry deployments outpace academic publication, and L5 self-improving ecosystems remain aspirational but within a realistic 2030 horizon.</jats:p>
title: Large Language Models and Foundation Models for Petroleum Engineering: A Survey

items.abstract: <jats:p>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an important development in the world of large language models (LLMs). By combining the ability of LLMs to generate text with access to external knowledge sources, RAG systems can answer questions and solve problems that require more than just what the model "remembers." As LLMs get better at reasoning, they allow RAG systems to handle more complicated tasks with higher accuracy and flexibility. In this survey, we carefully explain what we mean by "reasoning" in the context of RAG, and we provide a clear taxonomy that organizes different types of reasoning and retrieval strategies. We also show how reasoning and retrieval can work together to improve each other: better reasoning can guide more effective retrieval, and better retrieval can provide more relevant information for reasoning. Finally, we discuss new trends and promising directions for future research in this area. Overall, this work aims to give readers both a conceptual understanding and practical guidance for building more capable and intelligent retrieval-augmented systems.</jats:p>
title: A Survey of RAG and Reasoning in Large Language Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>Foundation models (FMs) large AI systems pre-trained on broad, heterogeneous data are increasingly embedded in scientific practice. Prior work has addressed this development in a piecemeal fashion: surveys of FM applications are confined to single domains, while reasoning taxonomies catalog general capabilities without mapping them to the full sequence of scientific work. We present FRAME-S (Framework for Reasoning with AI Models in Science), a four-dimensional framework characterising how foundation models reason scientifically. The four dimensions are Formal Reasoning (deductive and symbolic inference from premises to conclusions), Relational Reasoning (analogical transfer of structure across scientific domains), Abductive Reasoning (hypothesis generation from incomplete evidence), and Multi-modal Evidence Synthesis (integration of text, images, structured data and simulation output into coherent inferences). Each dimension is grounded in the philosophy of scientific method and mapped to the complete discovery lifecycle. We situate FRAME-S within a three-stage model of scientific paradigm evolution, propose reasoning transition thresholds specifying what a system must achieve to move between stages, derive five design principles with an operationalisation protocol for each dimension, and provide formal mathematical definitions specifying measurable properties. An empirical benchmark analysis applying the framework to published performance data for seven frontier models spanning 2023--2024 demonstrates that the four dimensions are empirically discriminable, that formal reasoning and multi-modal synthesis scale at markedly different rates, and that the Stage 1-to-2 formal reasoning threshold has been crossed by reasoning-specialised models.</jats:p>
title: FRAME-S: A Conceptual Framework for Scientific Reasoning with Foundation Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper provides an overview of the recent advancements in foundation models and discusses potential applications of these models in the field of biometrics. Foundation models (such as large language models, vision language models, audio-language models, and large multi-modal models) are based on large neural networks which are trained with massive amounts of data and enable robust feature extraction for transfer learning. These models allow efficient zero-shot and few-shot learning, achieving state-of-the-art performance in downstream tasks. Foundation models have been studied and used in different domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, audio processing, and multi-modal processing. Biometrics is also an active field of research, which involves various research problems, ranging from robust recognition to security and privacy in biometric systems. In this paper, we present an in-depth analysis of state-of-the-art methodologies regarding foundation multi-modal models, their advancements, and their applicability to biometrics tasks. We also highlight current limitations and provide insights into potential future research directions in the applications of foundation models in biometrics. To our knowledge, this paper is the first survey which investigates the applications of foundation models in biometrics.</jats:p>
title: Foundation Models and Biometrics: A Survey and Outlook
